items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Same eggs. Same store. Five different prices.
Narrator
Researchers checked a dozen eggs from one Safeway on Instacart, and shoppers saw three ninety-nine, four twenty-eight, four fifty-nine, four sixty-nine, or four seventy-nine.
Narrator
The study found nearly three in four items were offered at more than one price.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Prices are... personal, darling.
Narrator
It's called dynamic pricing: the price moves with demand, the time, or who's looking.
Narrator
Airlines already do it. Delta said A I set fares on about three percent of its domestic flights, with plans for up to twenty percent.
Narrator
Instacart ended its price tests in December twenty twenty-five, after the backlash.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the price tag looks fixed, but it can be an experiment.
Narrator
Before a big purchase, compare the price on another app, another device, or in the store.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky, high-pitched] So someone else paid less for the same eggs?
Narrator
Comment: have you ever seen a price change while you were shopping?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
